subject: Post-demo: NovaCX model-fit & prompt collection - action plan
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: NovaCX model-fit & prompt collection - action plan

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful to see the NovaCX routing rules and the sample transcripts. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap:
- Primary use: automated triage + suggested response drafts for Tier 1 agents (customer support).
- Data sensitivity: transcripts include PII (emails, phone numbers) and occasionally payment references — you flagged redaction requirements and audit logging.
- Traffic profile: ~3k LLM calls/day initially (bursty around 9–11am PST), target 95th latency < 250ms for suggestions.
- Quality constraints: prefer zero/regression tolerance on hallucinations for compliance-critical intents.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) NovaCX: fill the attached prompt collection CSV with ~50 representative prompts (mix of happy path + edge cases) and mark required redactions. See template: novacx_prompt_template.csv (attached).
2) Redwood: run an initial eval using those prompts on the recommended model variants and share a short benchmark (latency, token cost, top-1 accept rate) within 3 business days of receiving the prompts.
3) Legal/security: Julian or your security contact — if you need an NDA before sharing raw transcripts, we can sign (we also accept sanitized/sampled prompts).
4) Pricing: we’ll provide a rough estimate for both hosted and dedicated modes once we see token distributions.

Attachments: novacx_prompt_template.csv (template for prompt + expected reply + metadata columns).
Internal links: redwood eval plan (we'll run the evaluation with our eval harness) — will share results and a follow-up call option.

If that sounds good I can coordinate a short handoff meeting (15m) to walk through the template with Monica from CS.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | (415) 555-0187

Hi Alyssa — all good questions. Short answers then a proposed plan: 

1) Raw vs synthetic prompts: either works. If you can share sanitized real prompts (recommended) we get a much better signal on model fit. If legal prefers, synthetic is fine for a first pass. We can sign an NDA.

2) Hosted vs Dedicated: we can absolutely run the initial eval on Hosted (no dedicated commit required). Hosted gives faster turnaround; for production Dedicated may be worth it if you prioritize predictable p99 latency and data isolation.

3) Edge-case checklist (high level):
   - Escalation signals (customer asks for refund, legal, or complaints)
   - Very short utterances ("Thanks", "Help")
   - Truncated sentences / ASR artifacts
   - Payment/PII mentions (masking/redaction required)
   - Multi-turn context where agent prompt includes previous messages

Recommended model variants to evaluate (initial pass):
- redwood-2-7b-quant (cost effective, good latency profile)
- redwood-chat-13b (higher quality on instruction-following; higher cost)
- open-chat-13b-pt (open-source baseline for comparison)

Plan & timeline:
- You: send prompt CSV (50 rows) + mark any prompts that contain PII.
- Redwood: run eval on Hosted across the 3 variants, produce a 1-page scorecard (latency, tokens, top-1 accept, hallucination flags) + notes on prompt tweaks within 3 business days of receiving the CSV.
- Follow-up 30m call to review results and discuss canary rollout/quality guards.

I’ve attached a short eval plan: redwood_eval_plan.pdf (shows methodology and metrics we’ll report).

Thanks — Monica will take ownership on the prompt template walkthrough once you’ve shared the CSV.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: NovaCX model-fit & prompt collection - action plan

Hi Alyssa — happy to run the template walkthrough. A few practical notes for the prompt CSV to speed evaluation and avoid back-and-forth: 

Required CSV columns (use the attached template):
- prompt_id (unique)
- user_utterance (the customer message)
- context (optional — previous 1–2 messages)
- expected_agent_response (what a correct suggestion looks like)
- severity_tag (low/medium/high)
- contains_pii (yes/no)
- redaction_notes (if contains_pii, how you redacted)

Redaction guidance (please apply before upload unless you want to sign an NDA):
- Replace emails with <EMAIL_REDACTED>, phone numbers with <PHONE_REDACTED>, account ids with <ACCOUNT_REDACTED>, payment references with <PAYMENT_REDACTED>.
- Keep sentence structure intact; only replace token substrings.
- For multi-turn contexts, include the minimal previous turn necessary to interpret intent.

How to send us the CSV:
- Preferred: Google Drive link with view + comment access (share with monica.patel@redwood.com).
- Alternate: SFTP drop (we can share details) or secure upload link behind NDA.

If you want, I can run a short import sanity check and return a few example rows back annotated with how they’ll be evaluated (helps highlight edge cases).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

[Attachment: novacx_prompt_template.csv (CSV, 2 KB)]
